title: Testing that callback resources are freed on GC: call fit first, then gc.collect
answers: how to test that a callback's listener is closed when garbage collected
body:
When a test checks that a callback releases its resources on deletion, run the callback through a real fit first, e.g. `MaxIterEstimator().set_callbacks(callback).fit()`. Hook-signature caching and the other code paths that can hold references only run during fit. Without fit, the test passes even when there is a leak.
Then do `del callback; gc.collect()` before asserting that the listener address is gone from sklearn/callback/_transport `_listeners` and `_message_consumers`.
The reference test is sklearn/callback/tests/test_scoring_monitor.py:test_scoring_monitor_listener_closed_on_gc. The test estimators live in sklearn/callback/tests/_common/estimators.py (MaxIterEstimator, MetaEstimator).
applies: Tests in sklearn/callback/tests asserting cleanup of callback-owned resources
